newsitem.title: UK: Last raw wool sale of 1996 ends on softer note.
newsitem.headline: Last raw wool sale of 1996 ends on softer note.

text.p: The last raw wool auction of 1996 saw steady to easier prices with a comparatively low clearance rate for the current clip of 79 percent, British Wool Marketing Board figures showed.
Halfbreds - used mainly in clothing - dropped their base level prices by two pence per pound.
Picks and Supers lost around two percent of their value since the previous sale on November 20, trading within a range of 99.5-102 pence per kg.
Carpet types fared slightly better with Red Kempy Welsh appreciating five percent while Swaledales gained one to two pence, selling for 92-93 per kg.
But the marginal improvement in carpet wool values failed to offset easing elsewhere and the overall price indicator lost one point to end at 105.
The total catalogue of 2.64 million kgs included just over one million kgs forward wool - a record proportion.
Around 78,000 kg of the next (1997) season's clip was offered for sale and almost 90 percent was cleared.
